166.t: Hardships in Texas and pool-shooting Rooster
166.s: Recalls shooting pool with Rooster and his traveling partner Quincy Forks.
166.ch: Los Angeles in 1935: school, jam sessions and the hobo trip west
166.q: No, we had some real hardships in Texas. That was like the year of Grapes of Wrath, like when -- the dust storms... (recording interrupted). End of Reel 1

166.s: Put off a freight train, he and other hoboes walked through a dust storm.
166.ch: Los Angeles in 1935: school, jam sessions and the hobo trip west
166.q: Well, we spent a little bit better than 24 hours trying to get out of Amarillo. Like, they had dust storms during that year, '35, which killed all the crops, you know. It was very bad; bad scene. We got on a train in Amarillo, freight, during that time you didn't have to get underneath the train.…

166.s: Black travelers were not allowed in Dalhart; a railroad detective and posse chased them.
166.ch: Los Angeles in 1935: school, jam sessions and the hobo trip west
166.q: So we got in, got ready to get out. He said, 'You have fifty cents, but you can keep it,' he says, 'if that's all you have.' So we got another train. Now, this kind of train

166.t: Riding a fruit train to Los Angeles
166.s: He rode a manifest train to California and jumped off near Lincoln Heights.
166.ch: Los Angeles in 1935: school, jam sessions and the hobo trip west
166.q: So we look up, and here comes this train. And gathered up speed coming down the -- see, the reason we was about four blocks, now we're about eight blocks, getting away from this fire scene. The train's doing about 60 miles an hour. And I ran to it. This was my first experience hobbing.

71.t: Riding a freight train to Los Angeles and a pool hall job
71.s: In 1929 he and a friend rode freights to Los Angeles; he worked in a tough pool hall, returned to finish high school, then worked at a rock quarry.
71.ch: Freight trains and first trips to California
71.q: I went, I played around Parsons until 1929. In 1929 I left home. Me and a friend of mine caught a freight train and rode all the way out to Los Angeles.

71.t: How they rode the freight trains
71.s: He describes riding inside, under and on top of freight cars at night, and being locked in a celery car until a Mexican man freed them.
71.ch: Freight trains and first trips to California
71.q: Yes. Sure. And we used to ride, we'd be on top of a car, sometimes we had to run. We didn't want to, we'd just catch the first car we could, maybe we'd get a box car. And if we wanted to get to a low car we might have to run fifteen box cars before we'd come to a low one. And we used to run on top…

400.t: Revisiting Hugo Street in Texas: the 1936 fair, Joe Louis fight, an Oklahoma guitarist
400.s: Returning to Texas, Hinton looks for the house where he stayed in 1936, when the band listened to the Joe Louis fight on radio and heard a guitarist from Oklahoma.
400.ch: Road memories, photos, neighborhood and church
400.q: Yeah, disco. He said, “We have a disco every Saturday” [laughter]. Now this is in 1936. We were down there when the World‟s Fair… when Texas had the World‟s Fair. That‟s when Joe Lewis fought Smelly, and Smelly almost killed him. We were there at this Fair, playing for the World‟s Fair, stayed at…

113.t: Riding freight trains back to Oklahoma
113.s: Broke, they rode freights from Nashville to Knoxville and back, dodging railway agents who shot at them, until an old landlady fed them and sent them home.
113.ch: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
113.q: Well, sometimes -- you know those oil cars, you know, got the ring around them, you know? We'd stand up and ride those. Sometimes there was an open boxcar and we'd get in the boxcar if they wasn't traveling too fast. And sometimes when the special agents were bad on those trains, sometimes they'd…

146.t: Riding a coal car under the coal to Cincinnati
146.s: They hoboed on a flat car buried in coal through a mile tunnel, then shared a boxcar fire and hobo meals in Cincinnati.
146.q: : Oh, we went on down there and caught one of those big freight trains comin' out of Florida or Alabama or somewhere, South Carolina... Yeah, Chesapeake. Chesapeake Bay. It was of them big-big, long trains, about 300 coaches on it, and it was running! We went down into and clean into the mountains,…

169.t: Hoboing toward California and put off the train at Amarillo
169.s: He and a friend hobo toward California, are thrown off near Amarillo, and he fails an audition for his sister at a dance.
169.q: wasn't a musician, no. But he wanted to go to California, so I figured here's a buddy to run with. But they put us off the train anyway, right outside of Amarillo, Texas.
